currentContext.business: Polycab manufactures wires and cables (W&C, ~87% of revenue) for infrastructure, power, industrial, real-estate and mobility customers, and Fast-Moving Electrical Goods (FMEG, ~7% of revenue) including fans, lighting and luminaires, solar products, switchgear, switches, conduit pipes/fittings and small domestic appliances for retail and commercial customers. It also runs an Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) division executing electrical infrastructure projects for government and institutional power customers. Products are sold domestically through an omnichannel dealer/distributor/retail network and exported to 94 countries.

currentContext.strengths: Market leadership in W&C: India's No.1 cables and wires company with 30-31% share of the organised market, scale nearly twice its peers, ~10,000 SKUs, and industry-leading EBIT margins|Well-footed FMEG player: scaled to Rs 20,693 million in FY26 at a 25% CAGR since FY2013-14, six-category portfolio with 5,200+ SKUs|Pan-India distribution network: 3,900+ dealers and distributors, 190,000+ retail outlets, 24-hour delivery system, omnichannel presence (e-commerce, modern trade, mobile app)|High degree of backward integration: 100% of C&W sales manufactured in-house, improving quality control, margins and supply continuity|Strong R&D capabilities: NABL ISO 17025-certified R&D centre developing eco-friendly and E-beam-irradiated cables via global polymer research collaborations|Quality/promoter-led management team providing long-term vision and stewardship, backed by an experienced, independent Board

inverters and expand into Hybrid Inverters and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to strengthen presence in distributed energy and backup power|Fans: transition portfolio toward premium and Directors, a CEO for the B2B Channel business, and a Chief Digital & Information Officer to support technology/digitisation-led scaling|Capital allocation: fund capacity expansion primarily through internal accruals while progressively increasing the dividend payout ratio|Polycab funds its capacity expansion primarily through internal accruals given its net-cash balance sheet, positioning the Company to self-fund future investments while continuing to deliver returns to shareholders. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend for the year, does not propose to transfer any amount to Reserves, and the Company has not accepted any public deposits. The Company also maintains enterprise-wide certification to ISO 9001 (QMS), ISO 14001 (EMS), ISO 45001 (OHMS), ISO 50001 (EnMS), ISO 17025, IATF 16949 and IRIS as part of its quality/operational-resilience commitment underpinning Project Spring.
currentContext.expansion: Polycab operates 26 manufacturing plants across India (including named sites at Halol & Daman, Roorkee, Nashik, Chennai and Bangalore), supported by 35 warehouses/depots and a corporate, EPC and Telecom office network. Under the five-year 'Project Spring' plan (to FY 2029-30), the Company plans to invest Rs 60-80 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years, focused on capacity expansion, backward integration, digitization and ESG-led initiatives. During FY 2025-26 it incurred capital expenditure of approximately Rs 14.8 billion, its highest-ever annual capex, directed primarily at capacity-expansion initiatives and funded through internal accruals given its net-cash balance sheet. In the Solar business unit, manufacturing capacity was scaled up during the year (string inverter production raised to 1 million units annually; Solar Box production raised from 25,000 to 60,000 units/month), and for FY 2026-27 the Company is targeting complete in-house manufacturing of its full range of solar string inverters plus the launch of Hybrid Inverters and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). Separately, Polycab has entered a major indigenisation programme for pressure-tight submarine cables for naval projects (destroyers, frigates, aircraft carriers), with long-term testing running until April 2027.
currentContext.mdna: India's economy expected to sustain growth momentum (GDP projected 6.5%-7.5% ahead) supported by infrastructure investment, policy continuity and favourable demographics, providing a resilient domestic demand backdrop|Global cables and wires market is structurally attractive, underpinned by grid modernisation and clean-energy investment in the US, EU, China and the Middle East, renewable capacity additions, data-centre/digital-infrastructure growth, EV adoption and urbanisation|Indian W&C industry demand growth is estimated at approximately 1.5x-2.0x real GDP, driven by power transition (T&D expansion, grid modernisation, underground cabling), renewable energy evacuation infrastructure, infrastructure development, real-estate/housing wires demand, a gradual revival in private capex, and structural formalisation favouring organised/branded players|Broader FMEG/electricals industry (fans, lighting, pumps, switches & switchgears) expected to grow at ~6-7% CAGR over CY25-29, driven by urbanisation, rising electrification and disposable incomes, premiumisation and adoption of energy-efficient/smart/IoT products; discretionary retail demand was mixed (weather variability, cautious spending) while institutional/commercial/project-led demand was stable|W&C segment growth in FY26 was driven by robust domestic demand, particularly government infrastructure investment in mobility and power, and steady real-estate activity; product mix shifted toward cables (over wires) on higher infrastructure/industrial demand|Commodity input costs remained volatile: copper supported by an Indonesian mining-landslide supply shock and structurally strong electrification/renewable/EV demand; aluminium supported by Middle East smelting disruptions and limited capacity expansion; PVC saw an initial correction followed by a supply-driven recovery tied to Middle East feedstock disruption; steel moved cyclically on trade measures; the rupee depreciated meaningfully against the US dollar over the year, adding to input-cost and margin pressure|International business growth was affected by Middle East tensions that impacted export sales in Q4, though management remains confident in the long-term export outlook given a healthy order book and supportive demand trends across renewables, power infrastructure, oil & gas and data centres|FMEG growth was driven by business restructuring, distributor/channel expansion, new SKU launches and brand-building, with the segment turning sustainably profitable after breaking even in Q4FY25|Polycab's international/export business carries a healthy order book with supportive demand trends, despite Middle East tensions impacting Q4 export sales|In EPC, Polycab is executing two key government-aligned infrastructure projects — BharatNet and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) — with execution under BharatNet commencing during FY26

risks.note: Copper, aluminium, PVC and steel prices were volatile through FY26 on supply-side disruptions (an Indonesian mining landslide, Middle East smelting/petrochemical disruptions) and demand shifts; as key cable/wire inputs, sustained volatility pressures input costs and margins despite hedging and pricing actions.

The Indian rupee depreciated significantly against the US dollar during FY26 (from ~85.5/USD in April 2025 to above 93-95/USD by fiscal year-end), driven by crude prices, capital flows and trade-policy shifts, raising import costs for USD-denominated commodity inputs.

Expanding US tariffs and non-tariff measures (anti-dumping duties, safeguard actions), alongside similar measures by other economies, are accelerating trade fragmentation and regionalisation of supply chains, which can affect export competitiveness and merchandise-export demand relevant to Polycab's international business.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East
risks.note: Escalating Middle East tensions disrupted aluminium smelting and petrochemical (PVC feedstock) supply chains during the year and directly impacted Polycab's export sales in Q4 FY26, evidencing the Company's exposure to geopolitical shocks in a key international market.

China's economy expanded only moderately (~4.5%-5.0%) amid real-estate-sector stress and local government debt concerns, while the Eurozone saw subdued growth (~0.8%-1.2%) with manufacturing weakness in economies such as Germany; a weaker global environment can weigh on demand in Polycab's international/export markets.

risks.risk: Dependence on India's infrastructure and government capex cycle
risks.note: Domestic W&C and FMEG demand growth is closely tied to sustained government infrastructure/capital expenditure, private-sector capex revival and real-estate activity; a slowdown in any of these domestic growth drivers would directly affect Polycab's core revenue base.

one-line thesis: Another blowout quarter: consolidated revenue +39% YoY, highest-ever quarterly PAT of Rs 796.7 cr (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8% (+70 bps QoQ), on a net-cash balance sheet (Rs 3,990 cr). Wires & Cables domestic grew +43% YoY (though volumes only low-to-mid-single-digit on a ~26% base, so growth is commodity/realization-heavy), and FMEG roared +71% YoY (10th straight quarter beating industry) led by solar inverters (>2x) with EBIT already at 8% — the FY30 Project-Spring floor. Exports dipped on the Middle East, but management guides recovery with a healthy US/Europe/LatAm order book. All medium-term guardrails (W&C 11-13% EBIT, FMEG 8-10% EBITDA by FY30, 1.5x-market volume growth) reaffirmed.

| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | ~Rs 8,210 cr (implied) | +39% | Absolute not stated in remarks; implied from PAT/9.7% margin |
| EBITDA / margin | ~Rs 1,130 cr / 13.8% | +32% | +70 bps QoQ |
| PAT (rptd) | Rs 796.7 cr (INR 7,967 mn) / 9.7% | +33% | Highest-ever quarterly PAT |
| Finance cost | Rs 80 cr | — | Other income Rs 104.9 cr |
| Order book (EPC) | ~Rs 10,900 cr (Bharat Net + RDSS) | — | Bharat Net Rs 8,000 cr (Rs 4,500 cr execution/3 yrs) + RDSS Rs 3,250 cr |
| Cash / net debt | Net cash Rs 3,990 cr | — | Capex Rs 320 cr in quarter |
> One-offs / distortions: Working-capital cycle temporarily at **15 days** (vs 45-50 normal) on LC-driven higher payables — will normalize back to 45-50. W&C domestic +43% YoY is realization-heavy (volume only low-to-mid-single-digit) on a very strong ~26%-volume base last year. Channel stocking was **below expectation** as copper/aluminium prices fell sharply in June (aluminium -18-20%, copper ~Rs 14,000→13,100). A 3-4% price revision was taken in the first fortnight of July.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume growth:** 1.5x market/industry growth (blend of volume & value), reaffirmed through FY30; FY26 delivered 18% volume growth as the reference.
- **W&C margin:** 11-13% EBIT medium-to-long term (Project Spring); Q1 at 13.3% (top of band).
- **FMEG:** grow 1.5x-2x industry; EBITDA margin 8-10% by FY30 (EBIT already 8% this quarter — running ahead, but seasonality caveated).
- **EPC:** sustainable operating margin high-single-digit (Q1 at 11%, above trend); FY27 revenue ~Rs 800-1,000 cr from Bharat Net + ~Rs 800 cr from RDSS.
- **Exports:** >10% of consolidated topline by 2030 (export growth to outpace domestic); "uncapped" opportunity, no hard target.
- **Working capital:** settle back to 45-50 days.
order book & pipeline: EPC order book ~Rs 10,900 cr: Bharat Net Rs 8,000 cr (Rs 4,500 cr new-infra execution over 3 yrs; started Mar; fibre already secured for full execution period — insulated from rising fibre prices) + RDSS Rs 3,250 cr. Exports: "very healthy" order book across US, Europe, LatAm; US ~45-50% of export turnover, Europe ~18-20%, Middle East ~20-24% (Oman/Saudi/UAE recovering). Data-center opportunity framed as Rs 20,000-25,000 cr over 6-8 yrs (1 MW ≈ Rs 3.5 cr of cable, 50-60% conventional / rest optical fibre); Polycab already supplied Vodafone Idea DCs (Mohali/Pune/South).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Wires & Cables:** +39% YoY (domestic +43%); volume low-to-mid-single-digit on ~26% base; wires (high-single-digit) outpaced cables (low-to-mid); channel > institutional; West > North > South > East. International declined YoY (Middle East). EBIT margin 13.3% (favourable mix + opex discipline).
- **FMEG:** +71% YoY, 10th straight quarter above industry; EBIT 8%. Solar inverter is now the single largest FMEG category (>2x YoY, but <50% of FMEG); order of size: Solar > Fans > Pipes & Conduits > Lights > Switchgears/Switches. Premium mix ~25% overall (fans 33%, lighting 38%) — a key margin lever alongside operating leverage on a low base.
- **EPC:** revenue Rs 307.7 cr (-11% YoY on milestone timing), profit Rs 33.8 cr, margin 11%. Milestone-linked; no full-year dip expected.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **T&D/grid capex:** CEA guides ~20,000-21,000 circuit-km/yr for FY26-30 (vs ~14-15k last 5 yrs); FY27 ~17,000 ckm, with 2,000 ckm already added in Apr-May. Rs 100 spent on T&D ≈ 15% cable content (high pull-through). Transformer peers' order books at ~2.5x revenue cited as a lead indicator.
- **Rooftop solar:** PM Surya Ghar Yojana + state/central incentives driving the solar-inverter engine; 2-3 year strong trajectory expected.
- **Data centres / defence / EV charging:** ~4-5% of demand today, flagged as a potential "another layer" of demand that could explode.
- **Manufacturing/private capex:** BSE-500 ex-BFSI committed ~Rs 11.6 lakh cr capex over next 12-18 months (metals, semiconductors, manufacturing, renewables).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Distribution depth as demand-aggregator:** ~90% of sales through channel with channel finance → structurally low receivables (~20-30 days) and reach into Tier 2/3/4 private demand peers can't easily aggregate.
- **Procurement strength:** secured Bharat Net fibre for the full 2-3 yr execution window, insulating EPC margins from spiking fibre prices — a scale/balance-sheet advantage.
- **Market-share gains:** ~3-4% share gained (per last quarter's 10-12 month read); replenishment speed lets Polycab run leaner channel stock (~20-25 days) than peers.
margins & cost dynamics: W&C margin is a function of four levers: (1) export contribution (a drag this quarter on Middle East), (2) wires-vs-cables mix (wires higher-margin, helped), (3) channel-vs-institutional (channel higher, helped), (4) operating leverage (muted this quarter). Net, margins were "supported" at 13.3% despite the export drag. FMEG margin (8%) driven by operating leverage on a low base + premium-mix step-up (25% overall). Cost-plus model on copper/aluminium — RM moves pass through with a lag; falling June prices dampened channel stocking.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capex Rs 320 cr in the quarter ("continued commitment to building capacity"); no specific FY27 capex number reiterated on this call (refer Project Spring roadmap). Watch: EPC milestone timing (Q1 EPC -11% YoY is timing, not demand) and data-center demand actually translating from estimate to on-ground orders.
capital allocation: Net cash Rs 3,990 cr; disciplined capital allocation emphasised. Capex Rs 320 cr funded internally. Continued investment in distribution, brand/A&P (rising in FMEG), product innovation and talent. No buyback/dividend specifics on this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Volume deceleration optics:** 3 straight quarters of modest volume (low-to-mid-single-digit) — management insists it's base effects + RM-price-driven de-stocking, not demand loss; verify over 10-12 months.
- **T&D/data-center timing risk:** an analyst pushed that CEA T&D targets have historically undershot (14k vs 23k), and 1 GW/yr data-center adds are too small to move a ~Rs 1 lakh cr TAM — execution/timing is the swing factor.
- **Export/geopolitics:** Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Iran-US) hit exports; resurfaced last week — recovery not linear.
- **Commodity volatility:** copper/aluminium swings drive channel stocking and near-term realizations; a 3-4% price cut already taken in July.
- **Margin sustainability:** FMEG 8% EBIT is at the FY30 floor already — seasonality could pull it back; W&C export drag persists.
management quality / tone: Confident, data-rich, willing to "agree and disagree" with skeptical analysts (T&D debate). Transparent about volume being modest and the reasons (base + de-stocking). Consistent reaffirmation of Project Spring guardrails rather than chasing the strong print. By-design refusal to split FMEG category revenues or give copper/Q2 price guidance. Macro preamble is thorough (Fed/BoE/RBI, oil, IMF).
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline +39%/+43% W&C growth is realization-led, not volume-led (volume only low-to-mid-single-digit) — commodity tailwind flatters the top line; watch volume as the true share signal.
- The 15-day working-capital cycle is a temporary LC/payables artefact, not a structural improvement — it reverts to 45-50 days.
- FMEG's re-rating is real: solar inverter went from 3rd-largest to largest FMEG category in a year and EBIT hit the FY30 floor 4 years early — but still <50% of FMEG and seasonality-exposed.
- Bharat Net fibre is fully pre-secured for 3 years — Polycab is NOT exposed to the current fibre-price spike, unlike fibre-buying EPC peers.
- Channel de-stocking on falling RM prices means reported sell-in likely understates true sell-out this quarter — a possible coiled spring if prices stabilise.

- **EPC:** revenue Rs 307.7 cr (-11% YoY on milestone timing), profit Rs 33.8 cr, margin 11%. Milestone-linked; no full-year dip expected.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **T&D/grid capex:** CEA guides ~20,000-21,000 circuit-km/yr for FY26-30 (vs ~14-15k last 5 yrs); FY27 ~17,000 ckm, with 2,000 ckm already added in Apr-May. Rs 100 spent on T&D ≈ 15% cable content (high pull-through). Transformer peers' order books at ~2.5x revenue cited as a lead indicator.
- **Rooftop solar:** PM Surya Ghar Yojana + state/central incentives driving the solar-inverter engine; 2-3 year strong trajectory expected.
- **Data centres / defence / EV charging:** ~4-5% of demand today, flagged as a potential "another layer" of demand that could explode.
- **Manufacturing/private capex:** BSE-500 ex-BFSI committed ~Rs 11.6 lakh cr capex over next 12-18 months (metals, semiconductors, manufacturing, renewables).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Distribution depth as demand-aggregator:** ~90% of sales through channel with channel finance → structurally low receivables (~20-30 days) and reach into Tier 2/3/4 private demand peers can't easily aggregate.
- **Procurement strength:** secured Bharat Net fibre for the full 2-3 yr execution window, insulating EPC margins from spiking fibre prices — a scale/balance-sheet advantage.
- **Market-share gains:** ~3-4% share gained (per last quarter's 10-12 month read); replenishment speed lets Polycab run leaner channel stock (~20-25 days) than peers.
margins & cost dynamics: W&C margin is a function of four levers: (1) export contribution (a drag this quarter on Middle East), (2) wires-vs-cables mix (wires higher-margin, helped), (3) channel-vs-institutional (channel higher, helped), (4) operating leverage (muted this quarter). Net, margins were "supported" at 13.3% despite the export drag. FMEG margin (8%) driven by operating leverage on a low base + premium-mix step-up (25% overall). Cost-plus model on copper/aluminium — RM moves pass through with a lag; falling June prices dampened channel stocking.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capex Rs 320 cr in the quarter ("continued commitment to building capacity"); no specific FY27 capex number reiterated on this call (refer Project Spring roadmap). Watch: EPC milestone timing (Q1 EPC -11% YoY is timing, not demand) and data-center demand actually translating from estimate to on-ground orders.
capital allocation: Net cash Rs 3,990 cr; disciplined capital allocation emphasised. Capex Rs 320 cr funded internally. Continued investment in distribution, brand/A&P (rising in FMEG), product innovation and talent. No buyback/dividend specifics on this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Volume deceleration optics:** 3 straight quarters of modest volume (low-to-mid-single-digit) — management insists it's base effects + RM-price-driven de-stocking, not demand loss; verify over 10-12 months.
- **T&D/data-center timing risk:** an analyst pushed that CEA T&D targets have historically undershot (14k vs 23k), and 1 GW/yr data-center adds are too small to move a ~Rs 1 lakh cr TAM — execution/timing is the swing factor.
- **Export/geopolitics:** Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Iran-US) hit exports; resurfaced last week — recovery not linear.
- **Commodity volatility:** copper/aluminium swings drive channel stocking and near-term realizations; a 3-4% price cut already taken in July.
- **Margin sustainability:** FMEG 8% EBIT is at the FY30 floor already — seasonality could pull it back; W&C export drag persists.
management quality / tone: Confident, data-rich, willing to "agree and disagree" with skeptical analysts (T&D debate). Transparent about volume being modest and the reasons (base + de-stocking). Consistent reaffirmation of Project Spring guardrails rather than chasing the strong print. By-design refusal to split FMEG category revenues or give copper/Q2 price guidance. Macro preamble is thorough (Fed/BoE/RBI, oil, IMF).
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline +39%/+43% W&C growth is realization-led, not volume-led (volume only low-to-mid-single-digit) — commodity tailwind flatters the top line; watch volume as the true share signal.
- The 15-day working-capital cycle is a temporary LC/payables artefact, not a structural improvement — it reverts to 45-50 days.
- FMEG's re-rating is real: solar inverter went from 3rd-largest to largest FMEG category in a year and EBIT hit the FY30 floor 4 years early — but still <50% of FMEG and seasonality-exposed.
- Bharat Net fibre is fully pre-secured for 3 years — Polycab is NOT exposed to the current fibre-price spike, unlike fibre-buying EPC peers.
- Channel de-stocking on falling RM prices means reported sell-in likely understates true sell-out this quarter — a possible coiled spring if prices stabilise.
